initial_observation.encounter_context: Admitted to the hospital after being involved in a car accident
initial_observation.chief_complaint: chest pain that occurred after the trauma
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: The patient had no history of positive family background or drug use. Vital signs remained stable. No complaints of dyspnea. Oxygen saturation was 98%. Physical examination revealed limited chest movement, decreased tactile vocal fremitus on the right side, dullness upon percussion over the right area, and decreased breath sounds on the right side.
known_prior_history: previous hospitalization at the age of five due to meningitis

evidence_items.source_text: The CT scout view findings demonstrated the presence of an opacity in the right lower hemithorax without clearly evident shifting of the heart towards the left side (Figure 1).

The CT scan revealed the presence of a predominantly fat‐containing mass with soft tissue components, measuring approximately 13 × 23 × 15 cm. This mass appeared to originate from the anterior mediastinum and extended into the right hemithorax, without a clearly evident shift of the heart and mediastinum to the left. The lesion did not reach below the diaphragm. The lower lobe of right lung exhibited almost complete collapse (Figure 2).
Through a right thoracotomy, the mass was entirely excised (Figure 3).

The histopathological examination revealed the presence of an encapsulated lesion comprising mature adipose tissue that contained islands of non‐neoplastic thymic epithelial cells (Figure 4). The final diagnosis was thymolipoma.
The patient experienced no postoperative complications and was discharged in excellent condition on the 11th day following the surgery.
